title: Kernel-choice entropy spike postmortem and curation
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: During a 2.5 hour window on 2026-02-24/25 a regression materially increased tail latency and token-cost for a subset of hosted generation traffic. Root behavior: sudden increase in 'kernel-choice entropy' — the scheduler began frequently re-ranking kernel candidates across requests, which caused latency amplification, KV cache fragmentation, and an unexpected capacity storm on a small fleet of workers.
impact: Observed 3x increase in p95 decoding latency for affected routes, token cost increased ~28% for those customers. Approximately 7% of requests hit >2s extra decode time; several high-throughput tenants experienced request throttling and automatic failovers to fallback models, triggering customer support escalations.
timeline:
2026-02-24 22:03 UTC: Scheduled scheduler heuristic rollout started (canary phase)
2026-02-24 22:20 UTC: Internal latency alerts begin for route 'text-generate-remix'
2026-02-24 22:27 UTC: Operator notices spike in kernel-selection churn metric (new telemetry)
2026-02-24 22:35 UTC: Autoscaler reacts to perceived queue growth; scale-up starts but thrash follows
2026-02-24 23:05 UTC: Rollback of heuristic to previous commit initiated
2026-02-24 23:17 UTC: P95 returns towards baseline but intermittent tail remains through 2026-02-25 00:30 UTC
2026-02-25 01:10 UTC: Post-incident triage begins; reproduction and deeper analysis scheduled
root_cause: A change to the scheduler's candidate-ranking scoring introduced a non-deterministic tie-breaker combined with stale kernel cost estimates for certain quantized attention kernels. This produced high selection entropy: similar requests would flip between kernels frequently. The frequent kernel swaps prevented effective KV cache reuse and prevented batching from stabilizing, which increased per-token overhead and tripped autoscaler heuristics. Contributing factors: insufficient canary telemetry for 'selection entropy' and missing explicit kernel-model compatibility manifests that mark some kernel/model pairs as discouraged under short sequences.
mitigations: Immediate rollback of the ranking heuristic to the previous stable commit
Emergency manual pinning of kernel candidates for top affected models to enforce deterministic ranking
Applied short-term rate-limits on high-throughput tenants affected while rollback propagated
Disabled speculative kernel probing in the scheduler for mixed-quant workloads
action_items: ENG: Add a 'selection_entropy' metric to scheduler telemetry and wire alerts (owner: Liam Chen, estimate: 3)
ENG/Infra: Build a kernel-model compatibility manifest and enforce at routing time (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 5)
ENG: Implement deterministic tie-breaker policy to prevent reordering-induced churn (owner: Mateo Alvarez, estimate: 2)
ENG: Extend KV cache warmup logic to prefer prior kernel affinity for 10s after selection (owner: Sophie Park, estimate: 3)
SRE: Canary the ranking heuristic behind a circuit-breaker that measures entropy and latency before full rollout (owner: Jordan Li, estimate: 4)
PM: Update release checklist to require 'selection entropy' gate for scheduler changes (owner: Nora Patel, estimate: 1)
DX/Docs: Publish guidance for model-quant pairings and known pathological kernels (owner: Marco Rossi, estimate: 2)
Support: Outreach plan for affected customers summarizing incident and mitigations (owner: Elena Park, estimate: 1)
Bench: Create synthetic workload reproducer for mixed-quant short-sequence workloads and add to CI (owner: Ben Zhao, estimate: 3)
verification_plan: Deploy canary with selection_entropy instrumentation to isolated fleet, run synthetic reproducer for 72 hours, verify p95 and token cost regressions are within 5% of baseline and entropy metric remains below threshold. After verification, gate full rollout behind entropy and latency SLOs.
follow_up_notes: We observed that mixed-precision attention kernels are more sensitive to short-sequence churn; this should inform future kernel affinity heuristics.
Consider a short-term conservative default that prefers older kernel affinity unless new kernels demonstrate clear cost improvement under current workload distribution.
Cross-team sync planned with Quant and Serving runtime teams to agree on manifest shape and enforcement policy (scheduled 2026-03-12).
